summary: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists Ramshorn Peak only as an unknown or undocumented site; no lookout history was found.

evidence.supports: Ramshorn Peak is listed in Fremont County with coordinates
The entry sits under the Unknown/Undocumented Sites heading, not with lookout structures
A site moves to the lookout lists only if evidence shows regular fire-lookout use
evidence.quote: If evidence or documentation is uncovered showing that any of these were actually used as regular wildland fire lookout sites, they will be moved to the lookout lists.
situated approximately 16 miles east of the Continental Divide in the Absaroka Range
It is set in the Washakie Wilderness

evidence.supports: Land managed by Shoshone National Forest
evidence.quote: on land managed by Shoshone National Forest

evidence.supports: Dubois is the nearest town, 16 miles to the south-southeast
First ascent of the summit on July 13, 1960
evidence.quote: The first ascent of the summit was made July 13, 1960

evidence.supports: Forest Service marker describes the Ramshorn as a plateau named for its escarpment
evidence.quote: The Ramshorn is one such plateau but its name derives from its escarpment

notes_for_editor: The FFLA Wyoming list files Ramshorn Peak under Unknown/Undocumented Sites, with no type or status. The record describes a peak, not a structure. No lookout, build date or staffing appears in any source found in two searches and the cached pages. Wikipedia describes a summit and the Forest Service marker a plateau; the story says so. The editor should decide whether a name with no documented lookout belongs on the map at all. Owner and current status of any structure are unknown. The Shoshone National Forest pages were not checked.
